title: Global Payments Now Owns Worldpay: What Merchants Should Know
description: Global Payments completed its Worldpay takeover in January 2026, adding it to takepayments. What it means for UK merchants’ contracts, terminals and switching.
h1: Global Payments now owns Worldpay: what it means for UK merchants
intro: One of the biggest payment deals in years completed in January 2026, putting Worldpay under the same owner as takepayments. If you use either, here’s what to know.

image.alt: A person holding a payment card while using a laptop

cardText: The Worldpay deal, takepayments, and what changes for you.

sources.title: Business Wire: Global Payments completes acquisition of Worldpay
takepayments: about us (a Global Payments company)

sections.html:
On 12 January 2026, US payments firm Global Payments completed its purchase of Worldpay from FIS and private equity firm GTCR, and at the same time sold its card-issuing business to FIS. The deal was first announced in April 2025. Global Payments says the combined business serves more than six million merchant locations worldwide.

In the UK, Global Payments already owned card machine provider takepayments, so two well-known small-business brands now sit in the same group.

sections.h2: What it means if you’re a Worldpay or takepayments customer
sections.html:
• Your contract stays in force. A change of owner doesn’t change the terms you signed. Prices and terms can only change in line with your agreement, usually with notice.
  • Watch your inbox: integrations of this size can bring new statements, portals, terminals or terms over time. Read any change notices carefully, as they may give you a right to end your contract without a fee.
  • Check your renewal date: large acquirers must remind small businesses before their minimum term ends. That’s your moment to compare quotes.

If you get quotes from Worldpay and takepayments, remember they now have the same parent company. For a truly independent comparison, include providers from other groups as well, such as Dojo, Teya, Barclaycard, Lloyds Cardnet, Elavon, SumUp, Square or PayPal Point of Sale. See all providers and how to switch.
